hints: Focus on what excess acidified dichromate does to each functional group, and count how many [O] each change needs.
Notice that water is formed only when an alcohol group is oxidised, so the 1 $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ in the equation tells you how many alcohol groups X can have.
Add up the [O] needed for aldehydes and for that alcohol to reach a total of 3[O], then check which structure fits.
walkthrough:
**Recall oxidation rules with excess dichromate**

Remember with excess hot acidified $\text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7$, primary alcohols go all the way to carboxylic acids, secondary alcohols go to ketones, and aldehydes go to carboxylic acids.

$$\text{RCH}_2\text{OH} + 2[\text{O}] \rightarrow \text{RCOOH} + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$
$$\text{R}_2\text{CHOH} + [\text{O}] \rightarrow \text{R}_2\text{CO} + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$
$$\text{RCHO} + [\text{O}] \rightarrow \text{RCOOH}$$

**Use the water to count alcohol groups**

Notice only alcohol oxidations make $\text{H}_2\text{O}$, and aldehyde oxidation makes no water. Since the equation makes exactly 1 $\text{H}_2\text{O}$, X must contain exactly one alcohol group.

**Use the [O] to count the rest**

That one alcohol uses 1[O] if secondary or 2[O] if primary. To use 3[O] in total, X needs extra aldehyde groups to make up the remainder, with each aldehyde using 1[O].

**Check option A**

Structure A has two $\text{CHO}$ groups and one secondary $\text{CH(OH)CH}_3$ group. That needs $1 + 1 + 1 = 3[\text{O}]$ and gives 1 $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ from the single alcohol, exactly matching:
$$\text{X} + 3[\text{O}] \rightarrow \text{Y} + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$

options.A: Contains 2 aldehyde groups ($2 \times 1[\text{O}]$) plus 1 secondary alcohol ($1 \times 1[\text{O}]$). Total $3[\text{O}]$ needed and only 1 $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ formed from the one alcohol. This fits the balanced equation perfectly.
options.B: Contains 3 primary alcohol groups and no aldehydes. Each primary alcohol to acid needs 2[O] and gives 1 water, so it would need 6[O] and give 3 $\text{H}_2\text{O}$, not 3[O] and 1 $\text{H}_2\text{O}$.
options.C: Is glycerol, $\text{HOCH}_2\text{CH(OH)CH}_2\text{OH}$, with 2 primary plus 1 secondary alcohol. It would need $(2 \times 2) + 1 = 5[\text{O}]$ and give 3 $\text{H}_2\text{O}$. This is over-oxidation compared to the equation.
options.D: Contains 3 aldehyde groups and no alcohol. It would need 3[O] but would form no $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ at all, giving $\text{X} + 3[\text{O}] \rightarrow \text{Y}$. The equation requires 1 $\text{H}_2\text{O}$, so this cannot be X.
